plan.scopeTarget:
BOTH, asymmetrically.

Composer (Creature Lab, lab-only, freely versionable): full scope. That means recipe v2, individuals, coat, skin geometry fixes, rig individuality and gait fixes, herd view and a lighting preset. It has the worst measured defects and the richest body plans.

Planetary fauna: appearance and phenotype only. Changes are confined to src/creature-model.ts (realisticIndividualCreatureGenome path only), src/fauna-appearance.ts and src/fauna-body-plan.ts, which are SHARED_PRESENTATION_FILES fed identically to both sides of tests/life-cpu-digest.test.mjs:32-35, plus the new pure module they import. This is what users actually see on planets, and it changes no catalogue identity, no frozen genome digests and no LIFE_FILE such as fauna-near-rig.ts or fauna-runtime.ts.

Composer-on-planet integration is out of scope: rig-slot rebind, dated posing, triangle tier, far renderer.

workPackages.title: Composer rig: individual proportions/allometry/carriage, motion desync, lateral-sequence footfall, zero-velocity soft swing, continuous foot pitch, gated cos arm swing, consistent many-legged pole, size-scaled idle

workPackages.changes:
Set COMPOSER_GRAPH_VERSION = 'fauna-composer-graph-2'. In buildComposerGraph, compute traits = composerIndividualTraits(recipe) and store graph.traits. poseComposer(graph, motion, time) keeps its signature and stays pure; it reads graph.traits. Do NOT add bones.

1) ALLOMETRY AND INDIVIDUAL LIMBS:
- legRadius (rig.ts:345) and the arm radius (:397, :409) are multiplied by traits.allometry.limbRobust × traits.limbRadius. The existing clamp of 0.055-0.16 × reach stays.
- headLength (:167) is multiplied by traits.allometry.headRel.
- LEG segment ratios (:129-135) are multiplied per segment by (1 + segmentJitter[k]) and renormalised to the original sum, so reach is unchanged. Fore and hind use independent jitter.
- metaTilt ± 0.04·variability·zLimb rad.

2) TORSO PROFILE (rig.ts:200-213; feeds bone sections, so the clearance at :234-252 refits automatically). Multiply by individual terms, each traits.torso.x × v scaled:
- chest ±10% h at u 0.7-0.9 (Gaussian, sigma 0.08);
- belly ventral yc sag ±8% h at u 0.5 (sigma 0.2), plus +4% per unit condition;
- rump ±6% h at u 0.1;
- waist ±8% w at u 0.3.
Withers stays a mesh-side dorsal lobe (WP3); do not duplicate it.

3) CARRIAGE:
- neck elevation (:301) + traits.carriage.neck;
- head pitch (:302-303) + traits.carriage.headPitch;
- tail droop (:273-275) + traits.carriage.tail.

4) FOOTFALL (verified bug). Touchdown happens at cycle = 1 - phase, because stance starts at phase 0 and phase = cycle + limb.phase. The quadruped table at :387 {hind:[0,0.5], fore:[0.25,0.75]} therefore yields LH 0, RF 0.25, RH 0.5, LF 0.75 (diagonal sequence).
- Change fore to [0.75, 0.25] (index 0 = side -1 = left), giving lateral-sequence LH 0, LF 0.25, RH 0.5, RF 0.75, matching fauna-locomotion WALK_PHASE_OFFSETS.
- Primate-like bodies (arms grasping AND head flat-face) keep the diagonal sequence.
- Fix the comment.

5) MANY-LEGGED POLE: for non-arthropod legs use one pole direction (hind-style +X) for every pair instead of switching at i ≥ nTorso/2 (:365, :392). Arthropod legs are unchanged.

6) SWING TRAJECTORY (pose loop around :783-792), in the body frame, with Ts = (1 - duty)·period:
- x(u) is a cubic Hermite from rest.x - stride/2 to rest.x + stride/2 with end tangents m0 = m1 = -speed·Ts. This gives world foot velocity 0 at both ends; today it jumps 0 → speed.
- y(u) = lift·16u²(1-u)², which gives zero vertical velocity at touchdown (today -0.68 to -0.89 m/s).
- Foot pitch = -0.35·sin(2πu)·sin(πu)·(u < 0.5 ? 1 : 0.4). It is continuous at u = 0.5 because both factors vanish there. Spike feet stay 0.
- Keep the existing clamp asin(contact.y / footExtent).
- Stance feet stay level and flat: no heel rise this round, so the stance sole |y| < 1e-6 test stays as is.
- Duty and lift take traits.motion.dutyDelta and liftScale, still under fitStride and the COMPOSER_MAX_STANCE_EXTENSION 0.985 cap.

7) MOTION DESYNC: the cycle phase gets + traits.motion.phase; the period × traits.motion.periodScale (applied in locomotionFor so fitStride sees it).

8) ARM SWING (:814):
- target.x += A·0.22·reach·cos(2π(cycle + limb.phase)), so the arm is opposite the same-side leg. Verify with the gait test: the L hand is furthest back when the L foot touches down.
- A = 0 for arms 'small' or posture < 0.4; A = 1 for grasping arms with posture ≥ 0.6, linear between.

9) IDLE:
- breathing period = 3.4 s × clamp((bodyLength/1 m)^0.25, 0.6, 1.8), with phase traits.motion.breathPhase;
- look and nod phases offset by traits.motion.lookPhase;
- idle look yaw is applied about world up at the neck base, then distributed along the neck bones in the torso's gravity-aligned frame (today it is bone-local, giving giraffe 5.9 deg).

10) Neutral traits (seed 0, allometry 0, etc.) must reproduce b8c00bf rest bones bit-identically. Walk poses differ only through items 4-6 and 8.
acceptance: The footfall test computes touchdown cycles from the poses (as probe.mjs does). Giraffe, rhinoceros and winged-ape-rhino give LH → LF → RH → RF; an ape-like quadruped gives diagonal sequence.

Swing: in the first and last 2% of swing, world horizontal foot speed is ≤ 0.1 × body speed, and touchdown vertical speed is ≤ 0.25 × the baseline (dinosaur 0.82, giraffe 0.89, rhino 0.68 m/s). Report the measured values.
Foot pitch: the max rotation per 1/400 cycle is ≤ 4 deg on every non-spike preset (baseline 16-25 deg).
Arms: dinosaur small arms move ≤ 0.02 m during the walk (baseline 0.128). An upright grasping-arm biped swings its L hand furthest back within ±0.05 cycle of the L touchdown.
Many-legged: every knee offset of a non-arthropod many-legged body has the same sign (trunked-centipede baseline flips at pair 4).
Idle: giraffe head yaw range ≥ 15 deg (baseline 5.9). The breathing period differs between the bird and rhino presets.
Desync: in a herd of 12 giraffes (variability 1, seeds 1..12), the pairwise correlation of left-hind foot height over 4 cycles at a shared time is < 0.9 for ≥ 80% of pairs. Seed 0 reproduces phase 0.
Allometry: with allometry 1, legRadius/reach at bodyLength 4 m is ≥ 1.12 × the value at 1 m. With allometry 0 it is unchanged.
Neutral identity: neutral-trait recipes with allometry 0 have rest bone positions and quaternions bit-identical to HEAD.

Contacts and clearance for 12 presets × seeds {0, 1, 7, 42} plus maturity 0.3: stance slip < 1e-6, stance sole |y| < 1e-6, joint/socket/segment error < 1e-8, torso and swing clearance > -1e-6, and max stance extension ≤ 0.985. Seek/reset exact-pose determinism (rig-independent:62) for 12 individuals × 4 motions. Bone counts unchanged (12-pair endpoint 113).

plan.compatibility:
RECIPE VERSIONING
- COMPOSER_RECIPE_VERSION moves 1 → 2. Decode accepts 'v1*' and 'v2*' and rejects v3 and above; the tests move from 'v2' to 'v3'.
- v1 text migrates with zero issues. All 26 v1 field values are preserved, and the 12 new keys take neutral defaults: pattern 'auto', marks 0, patternScale 1, patternContrast 1, countershade 0.8, dimorphism 0, variability 0, allometry 0, individualSeed 0, sex 'auto', maturity 1, condition 0.
- A v1 text that equals a v1 preset's 26 fields adopts that preset's v2 species values, so old preset links still read 'Giraffe-like'.
- Encode always writes v2. The measured encoding cap is 377 of 1,200 characters; the target is ≤ 650.

DETERMINISM STREAMS (existing ones byte-identical; new ones append-only)
- Unchanged: 'composer-random-v1/<seed>' with its draw order, 'composer-colour/<palette>/<colorSeed>', and the composerHash/composerRandom primitives.
- New: 'composer-individual-v2/<speciesHash>/<individualSeed>', 'composer-species-v1/<seed>', 'composer-skin-ind-v1/<driftKey>', 'coat-species-v1/<palette>/<seed>', 'coat-individual-v1/<key>', and the planet channels '<speciesKey>/coat-v2', 'coat-lineage-v2', '<key>/sex-v2', '<key>/maturity-v2', '<speciesKey>/dimorphism-v2'.
- The coat field uses integer Math.imul lattice hashing, so CPU results are exact and there is no GPU dependency; coats remain vertex colours.

rationale:
I started from P1 because it has the best ratio of measured variation gain to risk. Its two foundations both reach the composer and the planet without touching frozen identity:
- recipe v2 with a species/individual split;
- a pure shared coat library.

On top of P1 I grafted the cheapest high-visibility realism fixes from P3 and P2. P1 alone would still produce toy-looking animals: the user asked for MORE REALISTIC as well as more varied, and the audit's top cross-cutting composer defects are geometric (helmet step, collar blobs, kinked joints, stick legs) and motion-related (wrong footfall, foot stomp, 16-25 deg pitch pops).

**Verified in the repo at HEAD b8c00bf, which shaped ownership:**
1. src/fauna-body-plan.ts is in BOTH LIFE_FILES and SHARED_PRESENTATION_FILES. lifeRendererModule applies sharedSources after the revision copies, so planet edits there are digest-safe.
2. src/fauna-near-rig.ts and src/fauna-material.ts are LIFE_FILES only. Editing them is a digest tripwire, so the planet shader path was rejected.
3. creature-lab-composer.ts types FIELD as Record<Key,string>, so adding recipe keys breaks tsc unless that file gets labels in the same wave. WP2 therefore owns that edit in wave 1, and WP5 takes the file in wave 2.
4. fauna-composer-mesh.ts types PALETTES as Record<palette>, so extending the palette enum needs a mesh edit in wave 1. WP2 gets a 3-line shim; WP3 owns mesh.ts in wave 2.
5. The swing code uses phase = (cycle + limb.phase), with stance starting at phase 0, so touchdown happens at cycle = 1 - phase. The current fore phases [0.25, 0.75] therefore give LH, RF, RH, LF (diagonal sequence), and the correct lateral-sequence fix is fore L=0.75, R=0.25.
6. The structure-independent test iterates a fixed key list, so new colour-only choices (pattern) do not break it. However, the 'legal numeric endpoints' test sets EVERY COMPOSER_RANGES key to min/max, so new numeric keys must stay buildable at their extremes.

**Rejected:**
- P2's pure-move refactor and its girdle/pastern bones: critical-path risk, IK and stance-test churn.
- P3's GPU shader: unverifiable under SwiftShader, Quest cost unmeasured, and it needs the near-rig LIFE_FILE edit.
- Planet SDF landmarks: grid budget.

**Waves.** Wave 1 holds the two foundation packages. WP1 must merge a tiny vocabulary commit first, because WP2 imports it. Wave 2 runs four packages on disjoint files: composer skin, composer rig, Lab, and planet. The coordinator runs an integration gate after wave 2, because the skin and rig interact through the floor and clearance tests.

perSpecimen.looksLike: Readable small theropod (Compsognathus/Dilophosaurus-like). The strongest composer preset.
whatBreaksRealism: The thigh is a thin tube with no drumstick mass. A theropod's femur and caudofemoralis bulk should make the hip the widest point. The leg looks bolted under the torso-tail junction.
The 'crest' is one flat, zero-thickness polygon plate that sits on top of the skull like a paper hat, with a hard edge and no blend into the skull.
The eye sits on top of the skull (dorsal), not lateral in an orbit. It has no brow ridge or lid, so the face reads blank.
'Jaws' has teeth drawn as 4 white tick marks, no lip line or gape, and the lower jaw is indistinct.
The torso shows visible faceting (low ring segment count). Stripes are smooth sine bands (mesh.ts:168 sin(q.x*22)), so they look like a lizard toy.
The metatarsus and 4 splayed toes are stick-thin and flat on the ground. There is no foot pad or claw mass.
Walk frame at t=0.55: the stride is a short shuffle and the feet stay nearly together.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A tortoise on stilts. The shell is good, the stance is wrong.
whatBreaksRealism: Legs come out of the shell vertically as long straight tubes, like table legs, and lift the plastron about one shell-height off the ground. A tortoise's elbows splay sideways and the plastron nearly touches the ground. The 'sprawled' layout does not sprawl.
There are hard visible seams where the leg tubes enter the shell rim (an elbow 'sleeve' edge).
The neck is a long uniform tube held horizontally out of the shell with no skin folds. The head is a faceted box.
The shell is a smooth dome with soft tonal bands. It has no scute polygons or growth rings and no marginal scutes.
Feet are round pads with 3 tiny white toenail dots, cartoonish.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A white llama or stick-figure giraffe. The coat reads as albino with dirt smudges.
whatBreaksRealism: The pattern is inverted. The savanna coat (mesh.ts:167) is mixC(belly, accent, 1 - smooth(0.3,0.4,cell)), so the dark accent only appears near Voronoi feature points as small specks on a cream body. A giraffe has large dark patches separated by thin pale reticulation lines.

The Voronoi is evaluated per vertex at q*9 (body-length units). The blotches come out as rectangular or star-shaped smudges that follow the triangulation (vertex-colour aliasing), not round-edged patches.
The legs are uniform thin sticks from shoulder to hoof. There is no forearm or gaskin muscle mass and no shoulder blade, and the upper and lower leg have about the same diameter.
The torso is a short box with no sloping back from withers to rump and no withers hump. The neck comes out of the torso's front top edge with no shoulder transition and keeps a constant diameter.
The head is very small and the ossicones are tiny yellow pegs. It has no ears worth noting, and the eye is a black dot.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A blue cartoon pigeon with paper wings and trousers. The weakest preset.
whatBreaksRealism: The visible leg includes a big feathered thigh and knee drumstick in body colour. On a real bird the femur and knee are hidden inside the body contour and only a thin scaly tarsometatarsus (keratin colour) shows.
Folded wings are crumpled flat slabs with jagged edges that stick out from the flank at angles, with pale yellow undersides showing. They do not lie along the body as a folded wing does.
The feather-fan tail is a zero-thickness plane. In side view it is a yellow fringe straight out of the vent, and in three-quarter view it collapses to a single line.
Posture is steep (posture 0.45) and the body is a tilted torpedo. The head is a separate grey sphere with a visible collar seam at the neck. The beak is a small cone.
There is no feather texture or body-contour feathering anywhere. The surface is smooth plastic with flat palette blocks.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A black long-necked stick creature or plesiosaur on stilts, not an ostrich.
whatBreaksRealism: The body is a small sloped sausage. An ostrich is a huge fluffy oval of plumage with white wing and tail plumes. Here the wings are a tiny pink shard on the shoulder (wingSpan 1.3 lands near the minimum) and the tail is a thin red line.
The legs attach at the extreme rear of the body, not under the centre of mass. The thick thigh plus long shank make an L-shaped crouch.
There are 4 long splayed toes. An ostrich has 2 toes and a large main toe pad.
The 'ink' palette makes everything uniform near-black brown. There are no bare pink or grey thighs and neck, which are the ostrich's key colour contrast.
The head is a tiny bead with a dot eye and a speck beak.

perSpecimen.looksLike: An ankylosaur-rhino toy. The head reads as a rhino, the body as a spiked reptile.
whatBreaksRealism: The 'osteoderms' armour is a regular grid of identical pyramids in 3 neat rows across the back. No rhino has this, and the even spacing reads as artificial.

There are no skin folds at the shoulder, flank or hip, and rhinos are defined by those armour folds. The torso is a smooth capsule with a hard break where the head block attaches. There is no neck mass or shoulder hump.
Hard shelf seams show where each leg tube starts at the body (a pale rim on the side view of fore and hind legs).
The tail is a thin stick ending in a huge black pom-pom ball. A rhino's tail tuft is small.
The colour is uniform flat grey with no wrinkling, mud or roughness variation. The ears are flat single-sided leaves.
colorSeed 400 and 7777 render pixel-identical. ImageMagick AE at 2% fuzz = 0, RMSE 0.10%.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A hunched dark mannequin or sloth-person rather than a gorilla or chimp.
whatBreaksRealism: The torso is a long narrow sausage with almost no shoulder breadth. The arms hang from the front of the chest, not from a wide shoulder girdle, so the ape barrel chest and trapezius mass are missing.
The legs are thin straight sticks under a heavy torso.
The feet (feet: hand) are giant flat pink human hands lying flat on the ground, bigger than the actual hands. The fingers are separated sticks.
The flat face has a disc ear stuck on like a headphone. There is no brow ridge or prognathous muzzle.

The body is matte with no wet specular sheen. There is no clitellum band, and the body tapers only at the very ends.

perSpecimen.looksLike: A sausage on 22 orange table legs, a toy centipede.
whatBreaksRealism: All 11 leg pairs are identical, go up and out and then bend 90 degrees straight down, and hold the body high. Real centipede legs sprawl laterally and backward, lengthen toward the rear, end in a long trailing last pair, and keep the body close to the substrate.
The body is a round cylinder with soft bands. It has no flattened tergite plates with overlapping edges and no paler sternites.
There are no forcipules or mandibles, and the antennae are two straight stiff sticks.
The walk frame shows almost no metachronal wave. The legs stay near-vertical.

perSpecimen.looksLike: Toy chimeras. Each one reads as glued-together parts rather than a creature.
whatBreaksRealism: Trunked centipede: 7 pairs of elephant pillar legs under a segmented sausage. The head is a rhino head with a long tube trunk whose tip lies on the ground. There are visible ring seams between segments.

Winged ape-rhino: the nasal horn on the flat face is a flat shield plate projecting from the face. Membrane wings are flat triangles slapped onto the flank, with dark spar streaks drawn through them. There are 4 hand-feet plus an extra pair of grasping arms held mid-air.
Shelled giraffe-bird: the dome shell sits on a cream body like a saddle, and the wing slabs poke out at the shell rim.
None of them has a part blend. Every junction (horn to face, wing to flank, trunk to snout) is a hard intersection.

perSpecimen.looksLike: Incoherent chimeras: a limbless grub with a trunk, horn and peacock fan; an upright 2 m biped with a 1.25 neck, flat face and broom tail; a turtle-shell biped with bat wings.
whatBreaksRealism: randomComposerRecipe (fauna-composer-recipe.ts:237-266) draws every part independently. There is no body-plan or ecological coherence: feather-fan plus limbless, trunk plus blunt worm head, dome plus membrane wings plus jaws.

audit-3 (biped, posture 0.04, tail none, legLength 0.97): the legs sit at the rear end of a 1.1 m horizontal body with no counterbalancing tail. The centre of mass is far ahead of the feet, so it is statically implausible. No balance or support check rejects it.

perSpecimen.looksLike: Padded is a clay dog or hyena puppy, winged is a deer with black bat-kite wings, and cursorial is a thin deer.
whatBreaksRealism: Padded: round spoon feet with no toe or pad definition. There is still a deer head, with one ear rendered as an edge-on blade.
Winged: the wings are flat black, zero-thickness triangles with 2 spar lines, stuck at the withers with a hard intersection. There is no wing musculature on the body.
Every family shares the same head template and coat logic, so a family changes limbs and appendages but not the face, skin texture or colour.

crossCuttingProblems: Surfaces carry no detail at any scale. Composer parts are vertex-coloured MeshStandardMaterial with constant roughness 0.82 and metalness 0 (fauna-composer.ts:45), with no normal or detail map and no fur, feather or scale microstructure. Everything reads as plastic or clay toy. The planet skin's procedural leg displacement reads as lumpy clay, not muscle or skin.

Patterns are limited by vertex-colour resolution. Spots, blotches and Voronoi cells come out as triangle-shaped stars and rectangles (giraffe composer, low-slung 'spots', runner 'stripes' with jagged edges). The giraffe pattern is also logically inverted (mesh.ts:167 puts dark accent only near cell centres). Real patterns (reticulation, rosettes, countershading, rump patches, facial masks) need a texture or shader-space evaluation, not per-vertex colour.

Parts meet with hard intersections and no blending. Crest, horn and ossicone plates, wing slabs, trunk collars, ear plates and leg tubes entering the body all show seams or shelves (composer rhino and turtle leg rims, bird collar, low-slung trunk collar, winged-family wings). Many accessory parts are zero-thickness single-sided planes: dinosaur crest, bird tail fan (edge-on it becomes a line), membrane wings, ears.

Limbs have no muscle anatomy. Composer legs are constant-radius tubes (no thigh drumstick on theropod or bird, no forearm or gaskin on giraffe, no shoulder girdle on ape). Bird knees are exposed outside the body. Sprawled and many-legged layouts stand on vertical pillars (turtle, centipede) instead of sprawling.

Feet and faces are generic and cartoonish. Toes and fingers are separated sticks (dinosaur, ostrich with 4 toes instead of 2, ape and winged-ape hand-feet larger than the hands), and pads have white dot toenails. Eyes are black dots with no lids or orbit, sometimes placed on top of the skull. The planet skin uses one muzzle, smile and nostril template for every family.

Individual variety is close to zero. A composer preset is one frozen recipe, and colorSeed only nudges base and accent hue ±0.03 and lightness ±0.05 (mesh.ts:131-139). Rhino colorSeed 400 vs 7777 is pixel-identical (AE 0 at 2% fuzz). On the planet, variant 0 vs 2 differs by RMSE 3-4% (coat shade, horn length). The juvenile is a uniformly scaled adult without neonatal proportions or a juvenile coat.

Random composition has no coherence. randomComposerRecipe samples parts independently (recipe.ts:237-266), giving grubs with peacock fans and trunks, and bipeds whose centre of mass is far ahead of rear-mounted legs with no tail counterweight. There is no balance, support or body-plan consistency check, so 'more variation' from this path produces absurd forms, not plausible animals.

Colour and palettes are too uniform. The planet browser base #685a46 vs belly #807058 gives almost invisible countershading. Composer palettes are 6 fixed hex sets with no age, sex or regional variation. 'ink' turns the ostrich and ape into black silhouettes, and 'savanna' makes a near-white giraffe.

Poses look stiff. The planet 'Standing' pose renders mid-trot with a scissored stance (fauna-skin-inspector idle override, t=2 s). Composer idle poses are rigid with no weight shift, head tilt or tail droop. The centipede walk shows almost no metachronal wave, and the dinosaur stride is a short shuffle. These are single-frame observations, not motion analysis.

Planetary fauna diversity is limited to one body plan. The default world's 12 species are all quadruped lineage across 4 archetypes, mapped onto 6 families on one shared 22-bone graph. The composer's biped, sprawled, limbless and many-legged plans are not used on the planet.
baselineVisualAudit.varietyAssessment:
Variety is weak in both systems, and this is measured.

Composer presets have no individual variation. The only per-individual input is colorSeed, which shifts base and accent hue by ±0.03 and lightness by ±0.05 (fauna-composer-mesh.ts:131-139).
- Rhinoceros (slate palette), colorSeed 400 vs 7777: ImageMagick AE at 2% fuzz = 0 and RMSE = 0.10%, so the renders are visually identical. Grey has no hue to shift, and stud placement does not change.
- Giraffe (savanna), colorSeed 400 vs 7777: RMSE 2.5%. Only the positions of the small brown specks move. Silhouette, proportions and horns are identical.

Seeded random recipes do differ a lot, but every part is sampled independently with no coherence, so the extra variety comes out as implausible chimeras rather than believable animals (capture-log.json lists the three recipes).

Planet skin individuals are slightly more varied but still near-clones:
- Variant 0 vs variant 2 (same species, adult, side view) gives RMSE 4.1% browser, 3.8% runner, 3.0% low-slung and 3.5% long-neck. Part of that is camera reframing.
- In the side-by-side variant 0 vs 3, the visible differences are slightly paler coat and shorter horns. The silhouettes are the same.
- Adult vs juvenile gives RMSE 8-11%, mostly scale. The juvenile is a uniformly scaled adult with smaller horns and relatively larger ears. It has no neonatal head-to-body or leg-to-body proportions and no juvenile coat.

Species-level diversity is limited to one plan: all 12 default-world species are quadruped lineage across 4 archetypes, and their heads share one face template.
